styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Shang dynasty ruins, the Yellow River and the Henan Museum.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Shaolin kung fu, ancient bronzes and temple courtyards.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Hui street snacks, noodle shops and night markets.

stays.why: Old downtown core. Walk to the Erqi Memorial Tower, street food and the metro interchange. Best for first-timers on a budget.
On the high-speed rail and metro. Handy for Shaolin Temple and Luoyang day trips, but few sights nearby.
Central business strip with malls, offices and mid-range hotels. Good metro links and plenty of restaurants.
Modern lakeside district around the big convention centre. Newer hotels, quieter nights, a short metro ride to the old centre.

food: Try Henan staples: hui mian (thick lamb noodles), hu la tang (peppery soup) and steamed dumplings. A bowl costs roughly ¥10–25.
Erqi Square and the nearby Dehua Street area are good for Hui (Muslim) snacks and evening street food. Prices are low; check hygiene on the day.
Zhengzhou is famous for hui mian noodle houses. Ask your hotel for a local favourite rather than a chain.
Night markets and food streets are busiest after 18:00. Carry small cash and expect crowds on weekends.
Tap water is not for drinking. Bottled water is cheap (¥2–3) and sold everywhere.
more_time: Add a day for Shaolin Temple and the Pagoda Forest near Dengfeng. It is a long day trip; check transport and ticket times on the day.
History fans can take the high-speed train to Luoyang for the Longmen Grottoes. Book seats ahead.
See the Yellow River at a riverside scenic area north of the city. Go in the morning; check opening hours on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Henan Museum, the Shang ruins and a Shaolin day trip; add a night if you want the Yellow River too.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 7°C, lows around -3°C. Pack a warm coat.
Still cold, highs near 11°C. Few rainy days; good for indoor museums.
Mild and pleasant, highs near 18°C. A good month to walk the old town.
Warm and comfortable, highs near 23°C. One of the best months to visit.
Warm, highs near 29°C. Light clothes; evenings still cool.
Hot, highs near 33°C. Sightsee early morning and late afternoon.
Hottest and wettest: highs near 33°C, around 12 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
Hot and rainy, highs near 31°C. Expect humid days and afternoon showers.
Warm and drier, highs near 28°C. A comfortable month for day trips.
Mild and clear, highs near 21°C. Excellent for walking and outdoor sights.
Cooler, highs near 15°C. Bring a jacket for evenings.
Cold again, highs near 9°C, lows around -1°C. Few rain days.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold, dry winters and hot, humid summers with the most rain in July and August.

items.title: Best time: April, May and October
items.text: Highs around 21–29°C and fewer rain days. Ideal for the museum, ruins and day trips.

items.title: Hot, humid summer (June to August)
items.text: Highs near 31–33°C with the most rain days. Plan indoor sights at midday and carry water.

items.title: Rain peaks in July and August
items.text: Around 12 rain days each month. Pack a light umbrella and a rain jacket.

items.title: Cold, dry winter (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 7–11°C and lows near or below freezing. A warm coat and layers are essential.

items.title: Clear autumn
items.text: September and October turn drier and milder, with highs of 21–28°C. Great for outdoor sights.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for spring and autumn, a warm coat for winter, light breathable clothes and rain gear for summer. Comfortable shoes for temple and ruins visits.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; Didi for late nights and sights off the metro lines.

modes.text: 7 lines, fares ¥2–9. First trains around 06:00, last around 23:00 (the Chengjiao line ends at 22:00). Cheap and easy for the centre and the station.
¥1–2 per ride with an extensive network and BRT lines. Cheap but slower than the metro.
Taxis: flagfall ¥8 day, ¥10 night, then ¥1.5/km after 2 km. Meters are used but watch for cheating. Didi works widely; Uber and similar international apps do not.
Not recommended for visitors: heavy traffic and complex rules. Use metro, taxis and Didi instead.
Central areas are walkable and shared bikes are available, but the city is spread out. Use the metro for longer hops.
